justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift assumption from what appears to be a baseline near 390–393 for the near-term SPY price. For the one-day horizon, I anchored close to the prevailing price level with only minimal drift, as daily moves are largely unpredictable and reversion tendencies dominate over such short windows. For the one-week estimate, I nudged the forecast slightly higher to 396, reflecting the long-run positive drift embedded in equity markets while acknowledging that a week is still a short enough window that drift contributes only marginally. For the one-month estimate, I pushed to 400, which represents roughly a 1.5–2% gain consistent with annualized equity returns prorated over a month, essentially assuming no major regime change and a continuation of the prevailing trend.

The confidence interval widths were driven primarily by historical volatility of the S&P 500. SPY has exhibited annualized volatility in the 15–20% range in recent years, which translates to daily standard deviations of roughly 1% and weekly deviations of roughly 2–2.5%. I applied these scaling rules to construct intervals that widen substantially as the horizon extends. The one-month interval is notably wide at plus or minus roughly 60 points because a month gives time for meaningful macro developments, earnings surprises, and sentiment shifts to compound. I also incorporated a slight fat-tail adjustment, meaning I widened the intervals somewhat beyond what a pure normal distribution would suggest, since equity returns are known to exhibit excess kurtosis and occasional gap moves.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals include a sudden deterioration in macroeconomic data — such as a sharper-than-expected jobs report or inflation surprise — that triggers aggressive Federal Reserve repricing. Geopolitical escalation, a credit event in the banking or sovereign debt space, or an unexpected earnings shock from a major index constituent could also produce moves well outside the 90% confidence bands. On the upside, a surprise dovish pivot from the Fed, a resolution of geopolitical tensions, or a strong batch of corporate earnings could push SPY meaningfully above the upper bounds, particularly at the one-month horizon where the compounding of positive news has more time to work through prices.
